Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation — moderate volume, controlled intensity; client should finish every session feeling worked but not destroyed.
Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Development — increased mechanical difficulty, unilateral loading, genuine pull-up volume; rest periods standardised at 2 minutes for main lifts, 90 seconds for accessories.
Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification — advanced bodyweight strength, plyometric elements, weighted pull-up simulation using a backpack filled with books.
Week 4 is a deload week: reduce volume by 30% (drop one set from every exercise), keep same movements, reduce tempo slightly — described as active recovery, not a rest week.
Week 8 is a deload week: same protocol as Week 4 — drop one set from every exercise, reduce intensity, move well and recover fully.
Dead Hang is described as an active exercise (shoulder packing and grip work), not a rest exercise.
Scapular Pull-Up described as the foundation of every pull-up; most beginners skip it.
Negative Pull-Up: jump or step to top position (chin over bar), then lower as slowly as possible — concentric is the jump, focus entirely on the descent.
Reverse Nordic Curl: use hands to push back up from the bottom; the eccentric is the primary work.
Week 3: begin attempting 1–2 full pull-ups at the start of Upper Body B before the negatives.
Ab Wheel Rollout substitution: if the bar cannot be used on the floor, substitute with a slow push-up lowering phase held for 3 seconds at the bottom.
Jump Squat note: 'Neighbours permitting' — plyometric impact acknowledged.
Dragon Flag: do not let the lower back arch; lower as slowly as possible.
One-Arm Push-Up Attempt: even one rep is described as a milestone.
Plyometric Push-Up: land with soft elbows.
Assisted Pistol Squat Week 6: reduce assistance — use only fingertips on the doorframe.
Week 7 Pistol Squat: attempt 1–2 reps with no assistance, use assistance for remaining reps.
Tempo notation explained as four digits: Eccentric – Pause at bottom – Concentric – Pause at top (e.g. 3-1-1-0).
RPE scale 1–10: RPE 7 = three reps left in the tank; RPE 9 = one rep left.
Recovery described as where adaptation happens; more training is not better for beginners.
Each muscle group receives roughly 48–72 hours of recovery between sessions.
Week 2: reduce rest periods by 10 seconds on all accessory work (exercises 4–6 in each session).
Phase 3 introduces weighted pull-up simulation using a backpack filled with books starting at 5–8 kg equivalent.
Weighted Pull-Up: if form cannot be maintained with weight, drop the weight and do bodyweight.

raw_text:
# 12-Week Home Strength Programme
### Client Profile: 27-Year-Old Male Beginner | Equipment: Yoga Mat + Doorway Pull-Up Bar

---

## Programme Philosophy

This programme is built around a simple but powerful truth: the body does not know the difference between a barbell and bodyweight — it only knows tension, progressive overload, and recovery. Every exercise selected here can be loaded progressively by manipulating leverage, range of motion, tempo, volume, and unilateral demand. Your client will move through three distinct four-week phases, each one deliberately harder than the last. By Week 12 he will be performing movements that most people in commercial gyms cannot do well.

The three phases are:

- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation** — Build movement quality, connective tissue resilience, and baseline strength endurance.
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Development** — Increase mechanical difficulty, introduce unilateral loading, and drive hypertrophy.
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification** — Push toward advanced bodyweight strength, high tension work, and peak performance.

---

## Training Structure

He will train **four days per week** on a Upper/Lower split. This gives each muscle group roughly 48–72 hours of recovery between sessions, which is optimal for a beginner making rapid neural and muscular adaptations.

**Weekly Template:**
- Monday: Upper Body
- Tuesday: Lower Body
- Wednesday: Rest or Active Recovery
- Thursday: Upper Body
- Friday: Lower Body
- Saturday & Sunday: Rest or Active Recovery

This structure is non-negotiable for beginners. More is not better. Recovery is where adaptation happens.

---

## How to Read the Programme

Each exercise listing follows this format:
**Exercise Name — Sets × Reps @ Tempo (Rest)**

Tempo is written as four digits: **Eccentric – Pause at bottom – Concentric – Pause at top.**
For example, **3-1-1-0** means 3 seconds lowering, 1 second pause, 1 second pushing, no pause at top.

**RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion)** is used on a 1–10 scale. RPE 7 means three reps left in the tank. RPE 9 means one rep left. This keeps him honest without a coach in the room.

---

---

# PHASE 1: FOUNDATION
## Weeks 1–4

### Goal
Establish perfect movement patterns in the push, pull, hinge, squat, and core categories. Volume is moderate and intensity is controlled. He should finish every session feeling worked but not destroyed. This phase builds the platform everything else sits on.

### Key Progressions Available in This Phase
- Slow the tempo to increase time under tension
- Reduce rest periods slightly week to week
- Add one rep per set each week where indicated

---

### WEEK 1

#### Monday — Upper Body A

**1. Incline Push-Up** (hands on a windowsill, desk edge, or sofa back — roughly 45 degrees)
3 × 12 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Why incline: reduces bodyweight load, allows perfect scapular control from day one. Chest, anterior deltoid, triceps.*

**2. Dead Hang** (from pull-up bar)
3 × 20–30 seconds (Rest 90 seconds)
*This is not a rest exercise. It is active shoulder packing and grip work. Tell him to pull his shoulder blades down and back throughout. This prepares the rotator cuff and lats for pulling work.*

**3. Scapular Pull-Up** (hang from bar, retract and depress shoulder blades without bending elbows)
3 × 8 @ 2-1-2-1 (Rest 90 seconds)
*This is the foundation of every pull-up he will ever do. Most beginners skip it and wonder why their pull-ups feel wrong.*

**4. Pike Push-Up** (hips high, body in inverted V, lower head toward mat)
3 × 8 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Overhead pressing pattern. Deltoids, upper traps, triceps.*

**5. Plank**
3 × 30 seconds (Rest 60 seconds)
*Squeeze everything: glutes, quads, abs. Body is a rigid plank, not a hammock.*

**6. Superman Hold** (lie prone, lift arms and legs simultaneously)
3 × 10 @ 2-1-2-1 (Rest 60 seconds)
*Posterior chain activation. Erector spinae, glutes, rear deltoids.*

---

#### Tuesday — Lower Body A

**1. Bodyweight Squat**
3 × 15 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Feet shoulder-width, toes 15–30 degrees out. Chest tall, knees track over toes. Full depth — crease of hip below top of knee.*

**2. Romanian Deadlift (Single Leg, Bodyweight)**
3 × 10 each leg @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Hinge at the hip, soft knee on standing leg, back flat, reach the free leg behind. This is a hinge pattern and a balance challenge simultaneously.*

**3. Reverse Lunge**
3 × 10 each leg @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Step back, lower the rear knee to within an inch of the mat. Front shin stays vertical. Glutes, quads, single-leg stability.*

**4. Glute Bridge**
3 × 15 @ 2-1-2-2 (Rest 60 seconds)
*Feet flat, drive through heels, squeeze glutes hard at the top for 2 seconds. This is not a lower back exercise — if he feels it there, his glutes are not firing.*

**5. Calf Raise (on a step or flat floor)**
3 × 20 @ 2-0-1-1 (Rest 60 seconds)
*Full range — heel drops below the step if possible.*

**6. Dead Bug**
3 × 8 each side @ slow and controlled (Rest 60 seconds)
*Lie on back, arms to ceiling, knees at 90 degrees. Lower opposite arm and leg toward the floor while pressing lower back into the mat. Core anti-extension work.*

---

#### Thursday — Upper Body B

**1. Push-Up (Standard)**
3 × 8 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*If he cannot do 8 clean reps, drop to knees — but only as a temporary measure. Perfect form over ego.*

**2. Negative Pull-Up**
3 × 5 @ 5-1-X-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*Jump or step to the top position (chin over bar), then lower as slowly as possible over 5 seconds. This builds pulling strength faster than any other beginner method. X means explosive — but in a negative, the concentric is the jump, so focus entirely on the descent.*

**3. Diamond Push-Up**
3 × 8 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Hands form a diamond shape under the chest. Triceps and inner chest emphasis.*

**4. Doorframe Row** (stand in doorframe, grip both sides, lean back, row chest to frame)
3 × 10 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*This is his horizontal pull. Retract the shoulder blades at the top. Rhomboids, mid-traps, rear deltoids, biceps. The more he leans back, the harder it becomes.*

**5. Side Plank**
3 × 20 seconds each side (Rest 60 seconds)

**6. Hollow Body Hold**
3 × 20 seconds (Rest 60 seconds)
*Lie on back, press lower back into floor, arms overhead, legs straight and raised. This is the foundation of every gymnastic movement and a brutal core exercise when done correctly.*

---

#### Friday — Lower Body B

**1. Wall Sit**
3 × 30 seconds (Rest 90 seconds)
*Thighs parallel to floor, back flat against wall. Isometric quad strength.*

**2. Step-Up** (onto a sturdy chair or low step)
3 × 10 each leg @ 2-0-1-1 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Drive through the heel of the elevated foot. Do not push off the back foot.*

**3. Lateral Lunge**
3 × 10 each side @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Step wide to one side, sit into that hip, keep the other leg straight. Adductors, glutes, quads in a frontal plane — often neglected.*

**4. Single-Leg Glute Bridge**
3 × 12 each leg @ 2-1-2-2 (Rest 60 seconds)
*One foot flat, one leg extended. Drive through the working heel.*

**5. Squat Hold (Bottom Position)**
3 × 30 seconds (Rest 60 seconds)
*Sit in the bottom of a squat and breathe. Ankle mobility, hip mobility, patience.*

**6. Bicycle Crunch**
3 × 12 each side @ controlled (Rest 60 seconds)
*Slow and deliberate. Opposite elbow to knee. No yanking the neck.*

---

### WEEKS 2, 3, AND 4 — PHASE 1 PROGRESSION

The session structure stays identical. Apply the following progressions each week:

**Week 2:**
Add 1–2 reps to every exercise where a rep range is given. Increase dead hang to 35 seconds. Increase plank and hollow body to 30 seconds. Increase side plank to 25 seconds. Reduce rest periods by 10 seconds on all accessory work (exercises 4–6 in each session). RPE target: 7–8.

**Week 3:**
Add another 1–2 reps. Negative pull-ups increase to 6 seconds descent. Doorframe rows: increase lean angle by stepping feet further forward. Wall sit increases to 45 seconds. Plank increases to 40 seconds. Hollow body increases to 30 seconds. Begin attempting 1–2 full pull-ups at the start of Upper Body B before the negatives — even if he only gets one, that is a win worth recording.

**Week 4 (Deload Week — but not a rest week):**
Reduce volume by 30% (drop one set from every exercise). Keep the same movements. Reduce tempo slightly — move a little faster. This is active recovery. The body supercompensates during deload weeks, not during the hard weeks. Do not skip this. By the end of Week 4 he should be able to perform: 15 clean push-ups, 5–8 negative pull-ups with a 6-second descent, 1–3 full pull-ups, a 45-second plank, and a 30-second hollow body hold.

# PHASE 2: DEVELOPMENT
## Weeks 5–8

### Goal
Increase mechanical difficulty significantly. Introduce unilateral lower body loading, harder push variations, and genuine pull-up volume. This is where real strength is built and where most of the visible physical change will occur.

### Key Changes from Phase 1
- Standard push-ups replaced by harder variations
- Pull-up volume introduced properly
- Lower body moves to Bulgarian split squats and pistol squat progressions
- Tempo remains controlled but concentric speed increases on some movements
- Rest periods standardised at 2 minutes for main lifts, 90 seconds for accessories

---

### WEEK 5

#### Monday — Upper Body A

**1. Push-Up with Feet Elevated** (feet on sofa or chair, body angled downward)
4 × 10 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*Shifts load toward upper chest and anterior deltoids. Harder than standard push-up.*

**2. Pull-Up (Assisted if needed — use a chair under one foot for light assistance)**
4 × 3–5 @ 2-0-1-1 (Rest 2 minutes)
*Full range of motion is non-negotiable. Dead hang at the bottom, chin clearly over bar at the top. If he cannot do 3 clean reps, use one foot on a chair for minimal assistance.*

**3. Pike Push-Up (Deficit)** (hands on two books or yoga blocks to increase range of motion)
3 × 10 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)

**4. Doorframe Row (Feet Elevated)** (feet on a chair, body horizontal, row chest to doorframe)
3 × 10 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*This is now a near-horizontal row — significantly harder than the Phase 1 version. Treat it like a barbell row.*

**5. Plank with Shoulder Tap**
3 × 10 each side @ controlled (Rest 90 seconds)
*From a push-up position, lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder. Minimise hip rotation. Anti-rotation core work.*

**6. Hollow Body Rock**
3 × 10 rocks @ controlled (Rest 60 seconds)
*From the hollow body hold, rock forward and back like a rocking chair. Maintain the hollow position throughout.*

---

#### Tuesday — Lower Body A

**1. Bulgarian Split Squat** (rear foot elevated on sofa or chair)
4 × 8 each leg @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*This is the king of unilateral lower body exercises. Front foot far enough forward that the shin stays vertical at the bottom. Lower the rear knee toward the mat. Glutes, quads, hip flexors of the rear leg.*

**2. Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight, Controlled)**
3 × 10 each leg @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Same as Phase 1 but with better control and greater range of motion now that he has the balance.*

**3. Reverse Nordic Curl** (kneel on mat, anchor feet under sofa, lower torso toward floor as slowly as possible)
3 × 5 @ 5-0-X-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*One of the most effective hamstring exercises in existence. The eccentric is the work. Lower as slowly as possible, use hands to push back up. This will be humbling.*

**4. Single-Leg Glute Bridge**
3 × 15 each leg @ 2-1-2-2 (Rest 90 seconds)

**5. Lateral Band Walk (no band — use slow, deliberate lateral steps in a squat position)**
3 × 12 each direction (Rest 60 seconds)
*Glute medius activation. Keeps knees healthy.*

**6. Dead Bug (with longer holds)**
3 × 6 each side, hold 3 seconds at full extension (Rest 60 seconds)

---

#### Thursday — Upper Body B

**1. Archer Push-Up** (wide push-up position, shift weight to one side as you lower, other arm stays nearly straight)
4 × 6 each side @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*This is a unilateral push-up progression. One arm does the majority of the work. Builds toward the one-arm push-up.*

**2. Pull-Up**
4 × 4–6 @ 2-0-1-1 (Rest 2 minutes)
*Same as Monday but aim for one more rep per set if possible.*

**3. Close-Grip Push-Up**
3 × 10 @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Hands directly under shoulders, elbows track back along the body. Triceps emphasis.*

**4. Chin-Up** (underhand grip — supinated)
3 × 4–6 @ 2-0-1-1 (Rest 2 minutes)
*Biceps contribute more here. A different pulling stimulus on the same bar.*

**5. Side Plank with Hip Dip**
3 × 10 dips each side (Rest 60 seconds)
*From side plank, lower the hip to the mat and raise it back up. Oblique strength.*

**6. L-Sit Hold** (sit on floor, hands beside hips, press down and lift legs — even a tuck position counts)
3 × 10–15 seconds (Rest 60 seconds)
*Hip flexor and tricep strength. Foundational gymnastics movement.*

---

#### Friday — Lower Body B

**1. Bulgarian Split Squat**
4 × 8 each leg @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*Same as Tuesday. Consistency builds strength.*

**2. Pistol Squat Progression — Assisted Pistol** (hold doorframe or pull-up bar upright for balance, lower on one leg)
3 × 5 each leg @ 3-1-1-0 (Rest 2 minutes)
*The pistol squat is the goal of Phase 3. This is the entry point. Use as little assistance as needed.*

**3. Step-Up (Explosive)** (drive up fast, step down slowly)
3 × 8 each leg @ 1-0-X-2 (Rest 90 seconds)
*Power development. The slow step-down is the strength work.*

**4. Glute Bridge March** (hold bridge position, alternate lifting each foot off the floor)
3 × 10 each leg (Rest 60 seconds)

**5. Calf Raise (Single Leg)**
3 × 15 each leg (Rest 60 seconds)

**6. Ab Wheel Rollout (using the pull-up bar on the floor — grip the bar and roll forward on knees)**
3 × 8 @ 3-0-1-0 (Rest 60 seconds)
*If the bar cannot be used this way, substitute with a slow push-up lowering phase held for 3 seconds at the bottom.*

### WEEKS 6, 7, AND 8 — PHASE 2 PROGRESSION

**Week 6:**
Add 1 rep to all pull-up sets. Bulgarian split squats increase to 10 reps per leg. Archer push-ups increase to 7 each side. Reverse Nordic Curl increases to 6 reps with a 6-second descent. Assisted pistol squat: reduce assistance — use only fingertips on the doorframe. RPE target: 8.

**Week 7:**
Pull-ups: attempt 5 sets instead of 4 on both upper days. Bulgarian split squats: add a 2-second pause at the bottom. Archer push-ups: increase to 8 each side. Pistol squat: attempt 1–2 reps with no assistance, use assistance for remaining reps. Reverse Nordic: 7 reps. Hollow body rock: increase to 15 rocks. RPE target: 8–9.

**Week 8 (Deload):**
Same protocol as Week 4. Drop one set from every exercise. Reduce intensity. Move well, recover fully. By the end of Week 8 he should be able to perform: 8–10 clean pull-ups, 15 archer push-ups each side, 10 Bulgarian split squats each leg with a pause, 3–5 unassisted pistol squats each leg, and 5 reverse Nordic curls with a 6-second descent.

# PHASE 3: INTENSIFICATION
## Weeks 9–12

### Goal
Push into advanced bodyweight territory. Maximise strength expression. Introduce plyometric elements for power. Consolidate everything built in Phases 1 and 2 into peak performance. This phase will challenge him seriously.

### Key Changes from Phase 2
- Weighted pull-up simulation using a backpack filled with books
- One-arm push-up progressions
- Pistol squats as a primary movement
- Plyometric push-ups and jump squats for power
- Higher weekly pull-up volume
- Longer time under tension on key movements
